notes: Baseline contamination (makes the delta CONSERVATIVE): subagents inherit this project's persistent memory, which names several real APIs from the Aug 2026 Skew work (registerSchema, lossyPaths, downgradedFrom, versionedFromContract, readResolving, envelopeFromResponse). The baselines used exactly those names correctly while inventing everything the memory doesn't mention. A true cold-start baseline (fresh machine, no memory) would score lower than 32.5%.

Failure pattern: baselines consistently get the CONCEPTS right (preserve 'ahead' data, no-store manifest, label lossy downgrades) but invent API surfaces that would not compile — versioned({name,version,steps}), provideSkewChunkRecovery(withChunkRetry(...)), skew-build CLI, { pinned: 1 }. The skill's measured value is API fidelity, not conceptual framing.

Two baseline behaviors are actively dangerous, not just wrong: eval-0 baseline CLEARS drafts on migration-chain failures (a shipped migration bug would destroy user drafts), and eval-1 baseline's buildId-equality check would auto-reload into the loop when a stale CDN region serves a different-but-OLDER build (the exact incident in the prompt). Both are failures the skill's rules section explicitly prevents.

Possibly non-discriminating assertions: "'ahead' not discarded" (eval-0) and "loss surfaced" / "rename+move+default op choice" (eval-2) passed in baseline runs too — the prompts and project memory leak enough concept for these. Keep them (they guard real regressions) but don't expect them to separate configurations.

Cost: with_skill averaged ~49.7k tokens vs ~38.4k baseline (+29%) and roughly comparable wall time (141s vs 124s avg) — the overhead of reading SKILL.md plus 1-2 reference files. Single run per configuration, so time/token stddevs are not meaningful.
